result.status: Done (D72). The lease page now authenticates and checks lease access before it returns any JSX. The data-heavy body streams inside Suspense. tsc and eslint are clean. I could only check the no-cookie redirect: it is a 307 to /login. I did not check a 404 for a real signed-in session.
checks_run: /tmp/claude-1000/pagecheck2.mjs does not exist, so I used the fallback. curl GET /leases/00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000000 with no cookie returned 307 to http://127.0.0.1:3000/login.
assumptions: I kept the async body component inside page.tsx instead of creating a new lease-detail*.tsx file, so there are fewer files to touch.

I left the ApiError 404/403 to notFound() mapping around getLease inside the streamed component as a fallback. The pre-check should make it unreachable in normal use, but if it ever fired it would run after the 200 was flushed and could not change the status code.

The extra getLease check costs one more lease lookup per page load: requireLeaseAccess and getLease each read the lease. I accepted that to keep the 404 a real 404 and to keep getLease's own authorization (R36).
The new LeaseDetailSkeleton in skeletons.tsx is my own layout: a header block, three summary cards and one table block. The task did not specify what it should look like.
No loading.tsx was added, per D61/D72.
